title: David Tennant
wiki_lead:
David John Tennant (né McDonald; born 18 April 1971) is a Scottish actor. His accolades include two BAFTA Scotland Awards, two Emmy Awards and nominations for three Laurence Olivier Awards. Raised in Paisley, Tennant trained at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland and began his acting career primarily working in theatre. His first major television role was in the BBC drama Takin' Over the Asylum (1994). He gained further recognition for the serials Blackpool (2004) and Casanova (2005), and appeared in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (2005).
A childhood fan of the science fiction series Doctor Who, Tennant starred as the tenth incarnation of the Doctor from 2005 to 2010. His portrayal is among the most popular interpretations of the character, and he returned as the Fourteenth Doctor in 2023. Tennant's further television roles include DI Alec Hardy in Broadchurch (2013–2017), Kilgrave in Jessica Jones (2015–2019), Crowley in Good Omens (2019–2026), Dennis Nilsen in Des (2020) and various fictionalised versions of himself in Staged (2020–2022). He is also a voice actor, voicing Scrooge McDuck in DuckTales (2017–2021) and the droid Huyang in the Star Wars series The Clone Wars (2012) and Ahsoka (2023).
Tennant has worked extensively on stage, including in Royal Shakespeare Company productions of As You Like It (1996), Romeo and Juliet (2000), Hamlet (2008–2009) and Richard II (2013, 2016); his Hamlet was adapted for television in 2009. He also starred in West End productions of Much Ado About Nothing (2011) and Macbeth (2023–2024). In 2015, he was the recipient of the Special Recognition Award at the National Television Awards.

Early life and education
Tennant was born David John McDonald in Bathgate, West Lothian, on 18 April 1971, the son of Helen (née McLeod) and Alexander "Sandy" McDonald. His father was a Presbyterian minister who served as the Moderator of the General Assembly of the Church of Scotland, and his mother was a charity worker. Tennant grew up in Paisley with an elder brother and an elder sister. Tennant was born with an extra toe on his right foot. He has suffered from acute anxiety since childhood.
Tennant's maternal grandfather was Derry City F.C. footballer Archie McLeod. On the genealogy documentary programme Who Do You Think You Are? in 2006, Tennant traced his maternal ancestry back to tenant farmers from the Isle of Mull and Ulster Protestants from Derry, Ireland.
At the age of three, Tennant told his parents that he wanted to become an actor because he was a fan of Doctor Who, but they encouraged him to pursue a more conventional career to ensure financial security. Nevertheless he was "absurdly single-minded" in pursuing an acting career. Tennant was educated at Ralston Primary School and Paisley Grammar School. grok_lead: David Tennant (born David John McDonald; 18 April 1971) is a Scottish actor renowned for his portrayal of the Tenth Doctor in the BBC science fiction series Doctor Who from 2005 to 2010. Born in Bathgate, West Lothian, Scotland, he adopted his stage name early in his career to distinguish himself in the entertainment industry. Tennant has earned acclaim across television, film, and theatre, with notable roles including the villainous Kilgrave in the Netflix series Jessica Jones, the demon Crowley in Good Omens, and DI Alec Hardy in the crime drama Broadchurch. His stage performances, such as Hamlet at the Royal Shakespeare Company and Macbeth at the Donmar Warehouse, have garnered Olivier Award nominations and Critics' Circle Theatre Awards for Shakespearean excellence. Tennant's career trajectory reflects a versatility spanning genre fiction, psychological thrillers, and classical theatre, contributing to his status as one of the UK's most recognized performers. He has received multiple accolades, including a BAFTA Television Award for Best Actor for his work in The Escape Artist and various theatre honors. In recent years, public attention has also focused on his outspoken views on social issues, particularly gender and transgender rights; during a 2024 speech at the British LGBT Awards, he criticized UK Minister Kemi Badenoch's positions on these topics, stating she should "shut up" and eliciting responses from political figures including then-Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, who labeled Tennant "the problem." This incident highlighted divisions in public discourse on sex-based rights versus gender identity advocacy.
